newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Diarrhoea kills scores in Bangladesh after storm.
newsitem.headline: Diarrhoea kills scores in Bangladesh after storm.

text.p: A diarrhoea epidemic has killed at least 64 people and affected more than 14,000 others in Bangladesh's cyclone-battered coastal region, health officials said on Saturday.

They said doctors and paramedics had been fighting an uphill battle against the disease in Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Noakhali, Laxmipur and Feni districts as well as on Kutubdia and Maheshkhali islands.
"Up to Friday, 64 deaths had been registered while the number of affected rose to 14,330," an official with the Health Directorate in Chittagong said.
"At least 43 people have died in Noakhali, 10 in Laxmipur, eight in Kutubdia and others elsewhere," he said.
Unofficial sources put the diarrhoea death toll at nearly 200 since the 200 kph (125 mph) storm from the Bay of Bengal ravaged the coast and islands on May 19.
Officials said the storm killed around 100 people, injured about 10,000 and left over a million homeless.
The disease broke out in the storm's aftermath as many survivors slept in the open, drank polluted water or ate rotten food before relief supplies reached them.
"Relief supplies have yet to reach many remote areas 11 days after the cyclone," a journalist in Cox's Bazar said on Saturday.
He quoted Dr. Belayet Hossain, civil surgeon in Kutubdia, as saying that many people were also suffering from dysentery on the island.
Thirteen medical teams including two from the navy were working in Kutubdia day and night trying to contain the diseases, Hossain said.
The government's public health department has installed hundreds of tube wells and repaired old ones to try to ensure a supply of clean water, officials said.
Army and navy were helping civil volunteers rebuildstorm-wrecked houses and build shelters, they said.
While fighting epidemics and hunger, people on the islands refuse after the storm.
"Many fishing crew have returned safely days after the cyclone, and we hope the rest will appear alive soon," one Maheshkhali islander told reporters on Saturday.
